#3153. Uber Eats starts drone deliveries with Zipline in Houston

Customers can choose "by drone" in the app, with Dallas and more US cities next.

Zipline’s delivery pod sets down an Uber Eats order. Houston customers can now choose “by drone” in the app.

Zipline has started delivering Uber Eats orders by drone in Houston, the first launch under the companies’ August partnership. Dallas comes next, and the pair are aiming for 1 million drone deliveries a day by 2029.

Uber Eats customers in Houston can now get food delivered by drone, Zipline announced on Tuesday. Customers pick “by drone” on the Uber Eats home screen, and a Zipline aircraft brings the order to their door. Dallas is next, followed by more US cities.

It is the first launch under the companies’ August partnership, which aims for 1 million drone deliveries a day by 2029. Uber also agreed to invest in Zipline, but did not say how much.

Zipline’s aircraft fly at up to 70mph and carry up to 8 pounds over 10 miles. They stay about 330 feet up and lower orders to the ground on a tether, which Zipline says keeps the noise down.

“Being able to reach people’s homes autonomously in under 10 minutes opens up a whole new opportunity for Uber Eats and its customers,” said Uber’s autonomous delivery head, Aaron Emrich.

Zipline says more than 80% of its orders are new business for restaurants, not orders they would have got anyway. It has made 1 million deliveries in the Dallas area alone.

Houston is not new ground for Zipline. In April, it opened early access there for the first 5,000 residents through its own app.

The drone delivery race is speeding up. Zipline raised $1.5B at a $21.5B valuation this month, as Walmart agreed to add 300 drone sites. Amazon plans to offer drone delivery in nearly 500 US cities and towns by the end of the year.

Food delivery rivals are moving too. DoorDash has unveiled its own drones, and Irish startup Manna is building a US drone factory in Oklahoma.

#3152. iPhone Duo now has twice as many optimized apps as it did 10 days ago

Apple marketing SVP Greg Joswiak said today that the number of iPhone Duo-ready apps on the App Store is twice what it was when Apple last reported the figure. Here are the details.

While it was obvious that the number of iPhone Duo-ready apps would increase over time, their limited availability was a big part of the conversation around early reviews and online commentary in the first days after the device launched.

That said, it was clear even from the early reviews that app updates were picking up quickly, with some reviewers having to rewrite or re-record parts of their coverage as more apps gained support for the device.

Earlier this month, Apple put a number to that progress when it announced it had surpassed 100,000 optimized apps.

Now, just 10 days later, that number has doubled, according to Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing, Greg Joswiak. In a post on X, he touted that more than 200,000 apps are now optimized for iPhone Duo, adding that he is “excited by how quickly developers have embraced” the device.

Over 200,000 apps are now optimized for iPhone Duo! That number DOUBLED in just over a week.I’m excited by how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and I can’t wait to see what they build next.

Joswiak’s update came on the same day that Apple released iOS 27.3 developer beta 2, which addresses two other common complaints from early iPhone Duo reviews: the lack of Face ID, and the inability to automatically lock the device when closing it.

As 9to5Mac covered earlier today, the second developer beta of iOS 27.3 introduces a new unlock option that uses the outer display’s camera to recognize the user’s face, as well as a setting to automatically lock the device when folded shut.

The latter addresses a common complaint from users who found it strange that closing the phone didn’t automatically lock it, requiring them to press the side button instead.

For more details on these two features coming to the iPhone Duo with iOS 27.3, follow this link.

#3151. Jensen Huang offers to return as Nvidia CEO if the board asks, CNBC reports

In a statement obtained by CNBC, Jensen Huang apologised to Nvidia’s board for the problems he caused. The board is not considering his return and is searching for a new CEO.

NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang during his GTC 2026 keynote at the SAP Center in San Jose, 16 March 2026

Jensen Huang says he would return as Nvidia’s chief executive if the board decides it wants him back. He made the offer in a written statement obtained by David Faber of CNBC on Tuesday. It is his first public comment since he resigned as chief executive on 12 November. CNBC’s Kif Leswing published the statement in full.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Huang said.

The statement landed hours before Nvidia reports third-quarter results, its first without him.

Huang apologised to Nvidia’s directors and said he would cooperate with the board’s independent investigation.

“I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret,” he said.

He said he had seen an outpouring of calls for his return from Nvidia staff, investors, business partners and customers. Many still contact him directly, he said. An open letter asking the board to reinstate him now has more than 180,000 signatures, CNBC reported. President Donald Trump said on Monday that he would not mind Huang coming back.

Huang also wrote about his own story. He came to the US 53 years ago. He called becoming an American citizen one of the proudest moments of his life. He described Nvidia as his life’s work.

Huang resigned days after admitting to an affair, CNBC reported. News reports alleged affairs with Nvidia employees and with Alice Huang, who worked for a customer and is alleged to have contact with Chinese intelligence.

Nvidia’s board is not considering bringing Huang back, CNBC reported on Monday. When he resigned, the board started a formal search for a permanent chief executive, according to Nvidia’s announcement. It will look at internal and external candidates. Colette Kress, the chief financial officer, is interim CEO. The board said on Friday it was choosing a search firm, CNBC reported.

Nvidia has hired the law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead its investigation, according to CNBC. The probe covers Huang’s conduct and whether it compromised national security or company secrets.

Huang has separately agreed to answer questions from three House committees on 1 December.

#3150. In My Cart: The best early Black Friday deals we’re buying today

The early Amazon Black Friday sale was just updated with a host of new discounts including the lowest prices ever across the Apple Watch Series 12 lineup, now even lower prices on AirPods Pro 3, and the return of the Apple TV 4K discount. You’ll find some deep on smart home upgrades for the holidays and some great ideas for stocking stuffers, intelligent helpers for around the house, and some great Apple gear gifts you can land for less than $20 a pop. For today’s early Black Friday edition of In My Cart, we have put together a collection of the gear we are picking up for ourselves – check it out down below.

Amazon updates early Black Friday sale with loads of new deals: AirPods, Apple Watch Series 12, Fold 8, PlayStation, more

It’s been over a year since AirPods Pro 3 were released, and I love them just as much now as I did on day one. The ANC is fantastic, the sound quality is great, and they’re incredibly comfortable. At their early Black Friday price, they’re even better. I’ve rounded up a couple bonus picks below as well.

Apple’s latest AirTag 2 in a 4-pack is an easy gift for the whole family and it’s now $79.99 on Amazon (just $20 per tag). I currently rock one with the FineWoven Key Ring. The longer Precision Finding range and louder speaker make it a worthwhile upgrade for those who frequently misplace things.

Ring doorbells and other home security products are seeing some sizeable discounts this year,with the battery version less than half-price and $100 off the wired 4K model. If you’re in the market for an affordable large screen TV, the Hisense 65-inch U6 Pro is less than half price, with a spec that includes 144Hz, Dolby Vision IQ and Atmos, HDR10+, and an anti-reflective screen. At a rather higher price point, Samsung’s 85-inch The Frame Pro is offering $800 off.

My picks are products I personally own or recommend as someone deeply invested in the Apple ecosystem. When I travel, anything that helps simplify packing is a win. The Anker Prime 3-in-1 charger is a great example: its compact, foldable design makes it an easy addition to my travel bag, and I can charge my iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods Pro with a single charger instead of packing three separate ones. And with Grand Theft Auto VI arriving this week, the new LG OLED evo C6 is a great way to bring the neon lights of Vice City to life.

I have a special someone who will be scoring a new Apple Watch Series 12 in Light Gold this year and with the price now at the lowest ever, it seems the perfect time to strike. I’m very much torn on whether or not I’m going to land the Dark Bronze for myself or not though – I actually really want the new Pearl White Ceramic model, but I’m having a hard time dropping that sort of cash down right now. Beyond that it’s a couple festive Yankee Candles for upcoming get-togethers and some other gear I’m waiting for the Black Friday deals on.

I’ve got a few upgrades on my Black Friday wishlist this year, and I’m curious to see just how low their prices will go. The eero 7 two-pack is a strong contender to replace my aging TP-Link Deco mesh Wi-Fi setup, while Samsung’s ViewFinity S8 could finally bring some much-needed resolution bump to my Mac workstation. I’m also eyeing Sony’s Midnight Black PULSE Explore earbuds, which have already hit a new all-time low ahead of Black Friday. And then there’s the Ember Smart Mug 3, which I’d happily swap my older model for, especially now that it’s dishwasher-safe and a lot easier to clean.

Three things I already use and would buy again are on my early Black Friday list. My blue UGREEN power bank matches my MacBook Air and iPhone 18 Pro, but the built-in retractable USB-C cable is what makes it so handy for charging an iPad without digging for a cord. A Withings scale is part of my regular routine, and Body Comp is the one I recommend in my smart scale guide. I also use Govee’s TV Backlight 3 at home, where it matches the glow behind the TV to what’s on screen.

My early Black Friday picks are all about clever gadgets that make everyday life a little easier. The Fanttik Cafein 11 combines two things I love, coffee and USB-C charging, in a portable espresso maker. For travel, the KeySmart SmartLock adds Find My tracking to a luggage lock, making it a more discreet alternative to tossing an AirTag in your bag. And Anker’s Nano Charger Neo Dynamic takes a similarly clever approach to something as simple as a wall charger, with 180-degree rotating AC prongs that let you point the USB-C port up, down, or straight out from the wall.

I’ve been spending the last few years trying to upgrade the home life of my parents after my mom’s spinal disability has severely slowed her pace and my dad has entered his 70s and is naturally unable to do what he used to. To start, there are some LEGO Botanical sets I’m picking up for mom, which she’s been getting into as a way to stay active when immobile, while also upgrading their cleaning routine with Roborock’s 2026 Qrevo S Pro Robot Vacuum and Mop, which is an advanced self-servicing model that keeps down into the accessible price range. From there, the outdated flood light atop their garage needs replacing, which is why I’m picking up the new Anker eufy 4K TrackLight Cam S1, which features a spotlight that tracks suspicious people until away and out of range, though this one isn’t seeing any savings right now.

#3149. Suno adds AI video to its music app, with filters for artists’ faces

Visuals makes lyric videos and album art for users' songs, but blocks prompts that copy real people.

AI music company Suno has launched Visuals, which makes images and video clips of up to 15 seconds to match users’ songs, including lyric videos that lip-sync. It is on the web now, uses separate credits, and comes with filters meant to block likenesses of artists, public figures and copyrighted work.

AI music company Suno has launched Visuals, a tool that makes images and short videos to go with users’ songs, it announced on Tuesday. Users can create lyric videos, album art and clips of up to 15 seconds. It is on the web now, with iOS and Android apps due in the next few weeks.

Suno says its video model is built around music. Clips follow a song’s structure, pick up on its lyrics and lip-sync to them. Users can start from Suno’s own characters or upload an image, then extend and edit clips with text prompts.

Visuals runs on its own credits, bought separately from song credits. It follows Suno’s Speech tool, launched in October for spoken audio such as poems and meditations.

New filters will block prompts and uploads that try to show specific artists, public figures or copyrighted characters, Suno says. Videos will also carry hidden watermarks before they can be shared outside Suno. ByteDance added similar guardrails to its Seedance video tool in March.

“This means that prompts that work on other video platforms may not work on Suno and that’s by design,” the company wrote.

Those guardrails come as Suno fights fresh legal battles. Last week, Elvis Presley’s music owners and Eminem’s publisher sued Suno, and the Presley suit claims it misused his voice.

Suno has been trying to look more legitimate. It launched music models trained on licensed songs from Warner and BMG in September, and plans audio watermarks for its tracks. Investors valued the company at $5.4B in June.

#3148. Best Black Friday Nintendo Switch deals in 2026 — LIVE updates from Tom’s Guide’s biggest gaming fans

Staff picked deals:1. Quick Links2. Editor's Choice3. Latest updates

Black Friday deals are ten days away. But don't wait around — early Black Friday Nintendo Switch deals are already popping up all over the web. This is the second day of our live Black Friday Nintendo Switch deals coverage, and I'm here to share the best of the best deals right as they appear — leading all the way up to the big event.

I'm a huge Nintendo fan myself, and I have a thousand hours racked up on my Nintendo Switch console to prove it. I'm also always on the lookout for price drops, because who doesn't like getting one of the best Nintendo Switch 2 games for less?

Welcome! We're a day closer to Black Friday and a day closer to full access to all the best Black Friday Nintendo Switch deals. In the meantime, I'm here to share the best savings with you live — so you can beat the rush and get your holiday shopping sorted before everyone else.

First things first... here's the best way to get yourself a Nintendo Switch 2 console right now. This bundle includes a Nintendo Switch 2, a copy of Mario Kart World and a 3-month Nintendo Switch Online membership. Compared to buying everything individually, you're saving $37.

We were hugely positive about this device in our Nintendo Switch 2 review, since it's just about the perfect upgrade from the original Nintendo Switch — with stronger performance, a bigger and better display and better controllers. You also get access to a stellar library of the best Nintendo Switch 2 games and the best Nintendo Switch games as well. Oh, and you can play everything at home on the big screen or on the go!

Something important to note here is that Nintendo has confirmed it will sell the Nintendo Switch 2 Mario Kart World bundle for $499 starting November 22. That's $50 off, saving you $80 in total — and bringing the bundle back down to its original, pre-price hike MSRP. But if you don't want to wait, or want to ensure you get one before they sell out, now is still a good time to buy.

One of the best Nintendo Switch 2 controllers we've tested has a sneaky hidden discount right now. It's the Turtle Beach Rematch, and it offers the same battery life as the Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller — while costing less than half the price.

This deal currently only applies to the black and yellow Super Mario Star variant of the controller (add it to your cart to see the discount.) You can also get the Invincible Mario variant pictured above on sale for $50.

Looking for a gift for someone who loves Animal Crossing: New Horizons on Nintendo Switch? Or maybe you're already a fan and are looking for your next obsession. I lovingly refer to Hello Kitty Island Adventure as the second best island-themed cozy game on Switch (behind Animal Crossing); it's one of the only games that has managed to scratch the same itch for me.

In this game, you'll jet off to a deserted island and work to rebuild it into a paradise. It's packed with quests to complete and lots of options for customization. Hello Kitty Island Adventure is continuously being updated with new content, features and events — and it's also super cheap right now as it's on sale for just $19.

Want to enjoy some intense soccer action over the holiday season? The latest game in the EA Sports FC series, EA Sports FC 27, is on sale with 50% off just ahead of Black Friday. I can't call it a surprising deal, but it's still a good one!

New to FC 27 is The Grounds mode, which lets you create an avatar and then take on the world in online matches. Otherwise, it's the same game that fans know and love. Compared to the other consoles, playing on Switch 2 means you'll lose a bit of visual prowess — and gain the option to play portably.

It's not currently on sale, but you don't want to miss this Nintendo Switch 2 game. I'm calling it: it's going to be the most popular and sought after Nintendo title this holiday. Our The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time review was pretty much nothing but positive, praising the game's gorgeous visuals and music, as well as the handy quality-of-life upgrades.

Want the best sound possible for your Nintendo Switch? The best gaming headset we've tested, the SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5, is on sale with $40 off right now. While it doesn't offer active noise cancelation, it ticks every other box — it's super comfortable to wear, the battery lasts up to 60 hours and you get 360° spatial audio that makes all your games feel even more immersive. The lowest price ever for these headphones is $79, but $40 off is still a good discount.

If you're looking for Switch game deals, Walmart is a good place to check. For example: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild is on sale for $46 at Walmart right now. This game is approaching its ten-year anniversary, but even today, it's still a must have for every Nintendo gamer. It'll keep you entertained well into the new year, since it offers dozens of hours of content — and it's cheaper compared to the shiny new Zelda release, Ocarina of Time.

Sonic X Shadow Generations is one of the best Nintendo Switch 2 games you can buy. And thanks to this discount, it's also one of the cheapest options on our best-of list. This title remasters one of Sonic's finest games, and adds new content to boot. The new levels feature a storyline focused on everyone's favorite edgelord — Shadow the Hedgehog. And the soundtrack in this game is so good that it's worth the price of admission alone.

If you own lots of Nintendo Switch game cards, keep them all organized in this case from Jsaux! It makes it easier to take all your favorites with you while you're traveling. There's space for 40 games in here, as well as MicroSD cards. And since Switch and Swich 2 game cards are the same size, this case works for both.

Super Mario Odyssey is great, but Super Mario Galaxy might be even better... and this deal gets you double the fun for a similar price. The excellent 3D platformers Super Mario Galaxy and Super Mario Galaxy 2 have been ported from Wii to Switch, and they feel better than ever to play now. With this Walmart deal, you can get them both in one package for $15 off.

Running out of space for your digital games? You can add more space with this 512GB MicroSD Express card from Samsung. It's currently 33% off and on sale for $99. The lowest price ever for this one is $74, but since storage prices are generally on the rise, that deal might not come back any time soon.

This isn't the biggest discount out there, but Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream is my second favorite game of 2026. (My #1 is Rhythm Heaven Groove, in case you were wondering.)

This game lets you make your own Mii characters based on whoever you want — then you simply observe all the mischief they get up to. It's not the most exciting thing you can buy, but I highly recommend a screen protector for your Nintendo Switch 2. It could be a lifesaver if you hate getting scratches on your console's screen! This deal from Jsaux comes with a pack of three, so you can share with a buddy (or have multiple attempts if you struggle with installation...)

Here's a deal I wasn't expecting! Pokémon Legends Z-A is on on sale for $20 off ahead of Black Friday. Although it released last year, it's still the latest title in the mainline Pokémon series and will surely be on a lot of wish lists this holiday. Amazon and Walmart both offer this deal, but you have to add the game to your cart to see the discount.

Check out our Pokémon Legends Z-A review, where our tester named it his favorite Switch 2 game yet. The new live battle formula is an excellent shake up for the series, and the story is extremely memorable to boot.

Feudal Japan is extremely fun to explore whether you're parkouring or riding your horse.

You play as Yasuke (a samurai) and/or Naoe (a shinobi), and their different fighting styles and tactics enrich combat. Conduct a frontal assault or hide stealthily while taking advantage of the shadows. Assassin's Creed Shadows runs well on the Switch 2, too, making this deal a must-have!

Overcooked! and Overcooked! 2 are two of our favorite couch co-op games — and the All You Can Eat edition which includes both titles is currently available for just $32 at Amazon.

In this (highly addicting) cartoon cooking simulator, you and up to three other players must cook and deliver dishes in quick succession — the quicker you are, the more tips you earn. Chop, dice, slice, steam, fry, bake, rinse and repeat, and don't forget to wash those dishes and put out the fires lest they burn your kitchen down!

Final Fantasy VII Rebirth is, without a doubt, one of the best JRPGs out there, and you can now play it on the Switch 2. We awarded the game 4.5-stars in our review, praising its incredible graphics, engaging storylines, fun combat mechanics, and huge worlds that are ready to be explored.

Wondering how the (formerly) PS5 exclusive runs on the Switch 2, especially compared to the PS5 Pro? Check out our article outlining the differences! And once you're done, don't forget to snap up this deal as soon as possible.

EA Sports FC 27 is the latest instalment in EA Sports' annual soccer simulation series. It adds a new "The Grounds" mode, alongside fan-requested upgrades to staple modes like Ultimate Team and Career Mode. It remains the most authentic recreation of the biggest sport on Earth you can play.

For soccer fans and Switch 2 owners, FC 27 makes for a great gift — and that too at 50% off? Who are we to say no to such a killer deal!

If you want an ergonomic controller that not only cradles your Switch 2 for a more comfortable experience, but also features the latest tech to give you a competitive edge, you need the GameSir G8 Plus. It's compatible with the OG Switch, Switch 2, Android and iOS smartphones, and tablets, making it an all-in-one on-the-go solution.

We gave this wireless controller 4.5-stars in our review for its excellent design (Marvel fans will love it), long-lasting Hall Effect triggers and sticks, and customizable back buttons. It features powerful rumble motors, too, to deliver an immersive gaming experience.

"Split Fiction is the best co-op game I’ve played since It Takes Two" is what one of our editors said in his review of the game. If you're looking for a genre-defying cooperative romp, Split Fiction should be your port of call.

It's creative, inventive, colorful, and downright delightful. The main story is compelling but so is the side content. For those who enjoyed It Takes Two, or even gamers who want a compelling game to play with their partner, get this deal as it saves you $14!

Not every movie tie-in game is great, but this pack is exceptionally good. In terms of licensed tie-in games, Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue and Toy Story 3 are some of the best around! Toy Story 2 is an excellent collect-a-thon platformer, while Toy Story 3 gives you a huge sandbox world that'll make you feel like a kid playing with toys again. Those two titles alone are great enough, but in this pack you get a bunch more games besides them to check out.

Nintendo has a family-friendly image, but don't be fooled — one of 2026's scariest games, Resident Evil Requiem, is right at home on Switch 2. This game is unique in the Resident Evil series since it can be played either in first or third person all the way through. The game's two protagonists offer two different styles of gameplay — you can swap between playing as zombie-fighting veteran Leon or FBI agent Grace depending on whether you prefer action or methodical exploration.

The lowest price ever for this game on Switch 2 is $49, but $10 off is still a nice saving.

Heads up: this is not a deal for the new Mario Kart game, Mario Kart World. It's for the last game in the series, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe. MK8D is the best selling Switch game of all time, and for good reason — it provides dozens of courses to race on and pretty much unlimited hours of fun. It's also the perfect game to play with family and friends over the holiday season. It's a lot cheaper than Mario Kart World, but it's just as enjoyable.

For the ultimate cozy gaming sesh this holiday — make sure you don't go without Animal Crossing: New Horizons. This is a game I can't stop going back to, because nothing beats the feeling of booting up New Horizons and checking in with all the cute animal friends on my virtual island.

There are no concrete goals to work towards in this game, but that's what makes it so great. You're free to take it easy as you catch up with your neighbours, decorate your island and catch critters with your fishing rod or bug net.

You might be wondering, what Nintendo Switch games am I playing right now? One of the titles I have in rotation is Story of Seasons: Grand Bazaar.

I still think Stardew Valley is the best farming sim on Nintendo Switch, but Grand Bazaar is a close second. The graphics look fantastic, performance is solid and the farming gameplay is just about perfect. It's so satisfying to make a huge profit selling crops at the weekly Bazaar — and seeing a run-down village transform into a bustling hub of activity along the way.

As well as storing your console and having space for game cartridges, this case has a built-in stand — making it easier to game in tabletop mode while you're on the go!

One of the Switch 2's big new features is the option to show your face on screen during gameplay (and Game Chats with your friends.) But you need a camera to make use of it — and the Piranha Cam is the one I'd pick up. Sure, its 480p resolution isn't the sharpest around, but it just looks incredible. Fans waited a long time for a new Metroid Prime game, and in our books — Metroid Prime 4: Beyond stuck the landing. Not only does the game look fantastic, the levels are packed with memorable details and the combat is excellent. It's not all perfect, as you'll have to spend a decent amount of time backtracking and traversing the desert overworld. But since the game is on sale for $43 right now, it's worth picking up.

This is a deal I think just about everybody should buy. Right now you can buy a $10 Nintendo eShop gift card for $8.98 at Amazon. That means you get a little over 10% off any digital game at the Nintendo eShop! The deal is limited to two per customer, but I definitely recommend grabbing it.

Metroid Ravenous is one of the most exciting Nintendo Switch 2 game releases set for 2027. If you want to grab a copy, you can lock your pre-order in and get $10 off the physical version at Amazon right now. In this game, it's eat or be eaten — you'll need to fight off monstrous adversaries and traverse a winding maze to help Samus Aran survive.

This is an underrated Switch game for sure. I rarely hear anybody talking about Advance Wars on Switch, but it's great! This is a strategy RPG where you'll need to use your tanks and soldiers to take control of the board. It's both challenging and addicting, with plenty of variety in terms of the types of missions you'll have to complete. The character animations and colorful, diorama-style visuals look great on Switch as well.

I know, memory has gotten more and more expensive in the last two years but you may want to expand the storage in your Switch 2. Digital games add up quickly.

Fortunately, the Samsung P9 Express microSDXC is on sale for what must be the best deal I've seen for a memory card in awhile. The 512GB version is on sale for $99 right now, down from $149. You can also get the 256GB version for $47.99 down from $79.

At this point, that's a steal and you should take advantage.

If you don't prefer the Joy Con 2 controllers then you need to pick up a standard controller.

8Bitdo makes excellent controllers and the Ultimate 2 Bluetooth Controller is on sale for $51.12. Plus, it comes with a charging dock in white or black. You can also use it with the Switch or your Windows.

We are highlighting deals today, but The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time just came out, and even at full price it's worth your time. The game was and remains excellent.

The remake is $69.99, but the digital version is a little bit cheaper. If you're like me, you prefer the physical edition.

The latest installment of EA Sports' annual FC 27 soccer series is pretty good, especially if you've skipped a couple of years. The new The Grounds mode is fun and similar to The Streets in 2K. It also has great upgrades to Ultimate Team and Career Mode.

Right now, it's on sale for the Switch 2 at exactly 50% off.

If you're a racer whether its Mario Kart World or something more intense, you have to give the Joy-Con 2 Wheel grip a try.

These aren't on sale but the pack comes with two wheel grips and at $25, it won't break the bank. Plus, it's just fun and makes holding the Joy Con 2 a little more comfortable.

If you don't mind refurbished, Target has a pair of the purple/green set on sale for $10 off the regular price. It's not a huge deal but it's a bit.

These are factory refurbished so they should be as good as a new set.

Nintendo will have its own Black Friday sale that kicks off on November 19 and runs through November 22. Specifically, starting on the 19th, a number of games will be on sale in the eShop.

Here's what you'll be able to get starting on the 22nd:

PowerA makes several protection cases for the Switch 2. Not all of them are on sale, but some versions include a Zelda Hyrule crest version.

The cases hold up to 9 game cards, 2 microSD Express Cards and come with an Integrated Play Stand.

I personally have the Pikachu case - on sale for $15.99 - and find it delightful.

#3147. Apple’s leadership overhaul continues with new Apple Pay and Wallet chief

Bloomberg reports that Apple lifer Corey Fugman will replace Jennifer Bailey as the head of the Apple Pay and Wallet division. Here are the details.

A few months ago, Bloomberg reported that Jennifer Bailey, Apple’s head of Apple Pay and Wallet, who had led Apple Pay since its launch in 2014, would retire in October.

At the time, Apple’s services boss Eddy Cue said internally that the company would announce its succession plan before her transition at the end of October, and that she would “continue to be available to support the transition in an advisory role.”

October came and went without any public announcement on that front. Today, however, Bloomberg reported that Apple has tapped Corey Fugman, “a 26-year company veteran as the new head of its payment service and digital wallet unit.”

According to his LinkedIn profile, Fugman joined Apple in September 2000 as Merchandising Manager for Apple Retail and has held several leadership positions since then, including overseeing Apple Card and Apple Cash from 2019 to 2021.

Most recently, he served as Senior Director of Apple Pay and Wallet, a position he has held since November 2021.

With the new job, Fugman inherits a crucial tap-to-pay business, which is estimated to generate billions of dollars a year. It handles tens of billions of transactions annually across more than 90 markets, with Apple taking a percentage.

The division also includes the Apple Card, which is transitioning from a partnership with Goldman Sachs Group Inc. to JPMorgan Chase & Co. Fugman has been highly involved with the shift to Chase, which is still ongoing, the people said.

The report notes that Fugman will report to Cue, and reaffirms that Bailey “will remain a consultant in the coming months,” echoing Cue’s earlier comments about her role in the transition.

Finally, Bloomberg adds that while Apple has undergone several leadership changes in recent months, including John Ternus replacing Tim Cook as CEO, Cue’s responsibilities have expanded considerably.

In addition to overseeing services such as Apple TV, Apple Music, Maps, and iCloud, Cue has recently taken charge of the App Store and Health following Jeff Williams’ departure as Chief Operating Officer and Phil Schiller’s decision to step down from overseeing the App Store.

#3146. Google buys Howie, an AI assistant that books your meetings

The scheduling agent was already built on Gmail and Google Calendar, and its team is joining Google Labs.

Google Labs has bought Howie, an AI scheduling tool that users copy into emails to arrange meetings, Bloomberg reported. Terms were not disclosed; PitchBook valued Howie at $14M in 2024. Google said it wants to build AI tools for small businesses with the team.

Google has bought Howie, an AI tool that schedules meetings and manages calendars, Bloomberg reported. Google Labs, the company’s experimental arm, announced the deal on Monday in a post on X. It did not share the price.

Howie works like a human assistant. Users copy it into an email thread, and it finds a time and books the meeting. PitchBook valued the startup at $14M in 2024, according to Bloomberg.

Google Labs said it wants to build “the next generation of intuitive AI tools” for small businesses with the Howie team.

Howie’s co-founder and CEO, Austin Petersmith, said the team will keep building the tool at Google. He noted on LinkedIn that Howie has always run on Gmail and Google Calendar. Google has not said whether Howie will be built into its own apps.

The deal adds to Google’s push into AI agents that act for users, not just answer questions. In May, it launched Gemini Spark, an always-on agent that takes tasks by email. In October, it gave workplace agents their own email addresses.

OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and xAI all offer rival agents, and OpenAI bought travel agent Odessia last week.

Google Labs has been busy. Last week it released Tabletop, a tool for building group planning apps with AI. In February, it bought music app ProducerAI, which runs on Google DeepMind’s Lyria model.

#3145. New iPhone Duo orders now deliver a month earlier than before

#3142. How Microcredentials Can Help Engineers Build Trustworthy AI

IEEE Credentialing Program pairs AI governance standards with microcredentials

Kaitlyn Ridel is the IEEE microcredentials marketing specialist.

Engineering teams are moving at breakneck speed to integrate artificial intelligence, but they are running into a formidable new barrier: compliance issues. Translating high-level AI ethics, governance, and auditing into daily operational workflows has become one of the industry’s toughest challenges.

“AI ethics” refers to the principles developers use to govern and operate workflows. “Governance” refers to the rules and procedures an organization establishes for AI workflows and how they interact with organizational data. Auditing is the process of assessing and validating systems to ensure safety, fairness, transparency, and legal compliance.

Technology leads and systems engineers are responsible for adhering to a structured set of guidelines for standards and processes usually issued by a governing body such as the European Union, the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, and the International Organization for Standardization.

The regulations aim to mitigate issues such as systemic bias, security vulnerabilities, and transparency risks, but they also highlight a critical skills gap.

Most traditional computer science, software, and electrical engineering degree programs were built around technical design and system architecture. They do not yet include training in AI auditing, data tracking, or safety protocols for how AI systems interact with people and other technologies.

Expecting mid-career engineers to leave their job to attend a full-time two- or four-year program to learn about the topics is not feasible. Yet treating safety and governance as an afterthought can lead to costly product delays, legal exposure, and broken public trust.

Targeted microcredential programs can bridge the knowledge gap by helping engineers build skills in compliance, AI ethics, and governance.

Skills-based microcredentials represent the mastery of expertise gained through a learning program. To earn them, learners must demonstrate the skill through a validation assessment. The microcredentials can be stacked, showing a growing skill set in a defined area and allowing learners to earn several microcredentials in one program.

Microcredentials also allow engineers to upskill and master critical competencies, such as bias mitigation, algorithmic transparency, and risk auditing, without interrupting their career. Through rigorous skills-validation assessments, microcredentials give tech leaders verifiable proof that their teams can audit systems effectively before deployment.

For engineering organizations, microcredentialing creates an agile upskilling pathway. It connects software engineering and hardware design directly to regulatory frameworks, empowering teams to certify systems for safety and compliance within their development life cycles.

Bridging technical capability and ethical responsibility requires a trusted foundation. IEEE has long been a pioneer in socio-technical standards, most notably through the IEEE 7000 series for ethics in AI system design, a framework created to address ethical considerations during the development life cycle.

The IEEE Credentialing Program translates the organization’s world-class standards into actionable, industry-aligned microcredentials. For more than three decades, IEEE has set the gold standard for technical validation and professional certification. By pairing cutting-edge AI governance standards with targeted microcredential programs, IEEE provides engineers and IT leaders with clear, standardized road maps to build systems that are not just technically advanced but also safe, compliant, and worthy of public trust.

To learn more about the credentialing program, explore the offerings or connect with an IEEE expert.

Kaitlyn Ridel is a marketing specialist for the IEEE Microcredentialing Program

#3141. Ambience’s AI now helps hospitals plan rounds and discharges

The new tools sit beside software that already writes notes and suggests billing codes.

Ambience’s new tools suggest tasks for each shift and flag barriers to discharge.

Ambience Healthcare has added Rounding Assistant and Discharge Readiness to its hospital AI software, to help care teams prioritise tasks and spot barriers to discharge earlier. The company also points to customer results on billing, including a 6.5% rise in case mix index at Onvida Health.

Ambience Healthcare has added two AI tools that help hospital teams decide what to do next for each patient, the company announced on Tuesday. They join its existing software, which writes clinical notes and suggests billing codes for hospital stays.

Rounding Assistant pulls together overnight events, changes in a patient’s condition and a list of suggested tasks for each shift. Discharge Readiness flags medical, practical and social problems that could delay a patient going home, earlier in the stay.

Ambience is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins and the OpenAI Startup Fund. It counts Cleveland Clinic and Mayo Clinic among its customers, and ties its fees to results. Cleveland Clinic has also backed Dyania, another hospital AI startup.

Much of the pitch is about money. Ambience aims to raise hospitals’ case mix index, a measure of how sick patients are that helps set what insurers pay. At Onvida Health, discharges handled with Ambience scored 6.5% higher than a year earlier, the company says.

“To justify the investment, we needed roughly a 1.5% improvement in case mix index,” said Mike Lewis, chief financial officer of Onvida Medical Group.

Lewis said Onvida’s own finance team checked the results. Ambience also says admission notes written with its tool captured 59% more of the diagnoses used in quality rankings, in one health system’s review of 1,100 stays. None of the figures come from independent research.

AI note tools are still under scrutiny. In August, England’s patient watchdog warned that AI scribes were getting drug names and diagnoses wrong. Rivals are growing fast too: Heidi raised $340M in September, and Google launched Gemini for healthcare last week.

For the last year, PC builders have been force-fed a very specific narrative about why buying a computer required a second mortgage. We were told that the AI data center boom was sucking up all the memory — resulting in 500% price surges.

And when news of a class action lawsuit against Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron broke in June, I was jubilant but fully expecting it to go nowhere, as this AI build-out was a good cover and the case hung on a “well, they’ve done it before” kind of prosecution.

But after a motion to dismiss got denied by the judge, who compared their synchronized supply starvation to “hawks flying in formation,” and the devastating new leaks about alleged GPU and memory shortage engineering, it’s becoming clear that something stinks.

This whole “RAMageddon” crisis is starting to feel like a deliberate squeeze rather than natural market evolution, and the fact that this entire artificial house of cards is currently collapsing under federal scrutiny is my definition of hopecore.

The big three memory makers — Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron — have been fighting this massive antitrust lawsuit alleging they formed an illegal oligopoly to artificially inflate DRAM prices.

Their defense was entirely predictable: they filed a motion to dismiss, claiming that their identical supply cuts were just the natural, independent reactions of companies surviving in a changing market.

And this week, Judge Noël Wise completely rejected that defense.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Judge Wise (which is a very apt last name) explicitly states that the plaintiff’s evidence is highly plausible following a staggering 500% price surge. The ruling highlighted that this wasn’t just a case of market leader leading and other following; it was a highly coordinated structural shift.

According to the court’s findings, the big three allegedly halted consumer DDR4 manufacturing and restricted general DRAM supply under the guise of an HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) data center pivot, while simultaneously adopting identical, highly unusual vetting procedures to verify end-customer demand.

Like my nephew who just got into playing Among Us says: "sus".

The Judge cited past legal precedent describing oligopolies as competitors watching each other “like hawks,” but noted this goes far beyond observation — ruling their synchronized supply starvation resembles “hawks flying in formation.” The companies now have until December 7 to officially respond to the complaint.

While the memory giants were allegedly fixing the RAM market, an entirely different kind of market manipulation has been allegedly happening on the GPU front.

In the fallout of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation, a damning new report alleges that the AI hardware shortage wasn’t driven by insatiable demand, but by an attempt to hide a massive oversupply. According to the leaks, Huang feared that Nvidia had over-ordered from TSMC and was about to be stuck with a mountain of excess enterprise silicon.

Instead of letting the market naturally correct (which would have dropped GPU prices), it’s alleged that Huang engaged in a massive “circular financing” scheme. Nvidia used its own capital to fund smaller neocloud AI startups, effectively paying them to absorb Nvidia’s excess GPUs.

It was an artificial demand loop, convincing the broader market that the AI hardware frenzy was still booming and keeping margins astronomically bloated across the industry.

Notably, the leaks vindicate current interim CEO Colette Kress. Rather than co-authoring the shortage, Kress, in her role as CFO, reportedly viewed the circular financing practice as highly toxic, actively challenging Huang’s bets and urging him to slow down.

This is why the RAMageddon Reset matters, and why you should absolutely refuse to pay inflated prices this Black Friday.

The exorbitant cost of PC gaming in 2026 wasn’t driven by an unstoppable technological revolution — more and more, it’s becoming clear that it was driven by white-collar collusion. But that era is over.

Smuggling rings and circular financing deals are being exposed and dismantled. And now, a federal judge is forcing Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron to answer for their synchronized price gouging.

The artificial floor holding up the PC hardware market has been kicked out from underneath their feet. As these companies scramble to avoid massive federal antitrust fines and DOJ indictments, they will be forced to flood the market with the supply they have been hoarding.

Hold the line, keep your wallet closed, and watch those prices fall. My prediction is still in play.

#3138. 28 Zero-Day Findings in Under Two Days. Is Robotics Security Keeping Pace?

VicOne’s AI-assisted research reveals what faster zero-day discovery means for robot safety

VicOne is a Physical AI cybersecurity company protecting vehicles and robots from cyber threats that can alter behavior and compromise safety.

VicOne used AI to find 28 zero-day vulnerabilities in Physical AI tools —these weaknesses can impact robot training, testing, and real-world control.

This article is brought to you by VicOne.

VicOne identified an initial set of 28 zero-day findings in less than two days using AI-assisted research across software and tools supporting the Physical AI ecosystem. These include projects developed or maintained by Google, NVIDIA, and Meta, among others.

Based on initial validation, all 28 findings are classified as zero-day vulnerabilities. The count may change following vendor and vulnerability-authority review, and some findings do not yet have CVE tracking numbers.

Many of these tools help teams train, simulate, test, and operate robots. Weaknesses in them could influence the models teams build, the test results they trust, and the instructions sent to robots.

These findings create two demands for robotics teams: responding as AI helps uncover weaknesses faster, and assessing how each one could affect robot safety and operations.

Vulnerability discovery involves examining code, tracing how systems communicate, and testing whether a suspected weakness can actually be exploited. AI can accelerate parts of this work, helping researchers analyze more software in less time. Attackers could use similar capabilities.

When the weakness is a zero-day — previously unknown and without an available fix — faster discovery can leave teams with little time to respond. While that exposure does not necessarily mean an attack has occurred, teams still need to determine whether they use the affected software and what an attacker could access or change.

VicOne’s findings span three stages of the robotics lifecycle: development and training, simulation and validation, and deployment and runtime. Weaknesses at each stage could affect what a robot learns, how it is tested, and how it is controlled.

Figure 1. In this research set, 75% of findings involved development, training, simulation, or validation tools, highlighting risks that can arise before a robot is deployed.VicOne

The following scenarios show how a compromised component could influence the robot at each stage.

These are potential consequences and not demonstrated outcomes for every finding. Actual effects depend on the attacker’s access, the system’s design, and whether other safeguards prevent the changes from reaching physical behavior.

In a separate demonstration, VicOne researchers provide a concrete example of a weakness affecting a protective function. The researchers exploited a vulnerability to prevent a robot’s remote-stop command from working. The case shows why teams need to test whether safeguards remain effective when the software supporting them is compromised.

Video 1. VicOne researchers demonstrate a vulnerability that prevents a robot’s remote-stop command from working. VicOne

AI can shorten the search for weaknesses, but a robotics team still needs to determine whether a fix is safe to deploy. Even after a software maintainer releases a patch, teams must identify affected systems, check compatibility, and verify that the update preserves intended behavior.

An earlier successful test remains useful evidence. However, a newly discovered weakness may reveal conditions that test never examined.

When immediate updating is impractical, teams may need temporary safeguards, such as restricting access to an affected service, while a validated fix is prepared.

As details from the 28 findings become available through coordinated disclosure, the next step is for robotics manufacturers is to connect each finding to its potential effect on development, deployment, and robot behavior.

That work also requires understanding how threats could affect robot behavior and how to protect systems already in operation. VicOne Radeis helps teams identify potential zero-day vulnerabilities, assess AI model and system security, and use simulation to evaluate how these risks could affect robot behavior before deployment. VicOne Rthena supports threat detection and responses within approved policies during operation.

Figure 2. Cybersecurity strengthens robot safety evidence throughout the lifecycle. VicOne helps teams test safety limits against manipulation before deployment and monitor the conditions behind safe behavior in operation.VicOne

Faster vulnerability discovery matters when teams can turn findings into action: identify what needs attention, verify that safeguards still hold, and confirm that a fix does not introduce new risks. That is how cybersecurity strengthens robot safety as systems continue to change.

#3137. Highwoods Properties: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

As tenant concessions expire and capital spending normalizes, free cash flow is poised to surge, potentially reshaping dividend coverage.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, Highwoods Properties (HIW -1.23%) raised its full-year funds from operations outlook, a standard metric tracking real estate cash generation. Capital recycling into top markets dictates the trajectory of property distributions.

Three statements from management reveal where the business is heading.

Highwoods Properties sells older assets outside prime submarkets to fund construction in premier locations. A low capitalization rate, which measures annual property income relative to purchase price, allows the company to harvest cash from mature buildings without adding heavy debt.

National construction of office space has dropped to historical lows. That supply shortage gives Highwoods Properties pricing power in Best Business Districts, or high-demand commercial hubs, where space is becoming scarce.

Upfront tenant concessions and building improvements hit short-term cash flow while building occupancy. As free-rent periods expire and capital expenditures, or cash spent on physical space, return to normal levels, net cash generation will surge.

Demand for premier office space is outpacing supply, driving higher rents across core submarkets. Executives are tracking pricing discipline as regional construction halts.

Disciplined capital recycling into prime locations positions the business for long-term growth.

#3135. Is IONIX the best-kept secret in cybersecurity?

AI is shrinking the time between a vulnerability’s disclosure and its exploitation. IONIX is building exposure management that finds, validates and mitigates external risks at machine speed.

As organizations expand their digital infrastructure, their external attack surfaces are becoming increasingly difficult to secure. Cloud environments, third-party vendors, subsidiaries, web applications and AI services introduce new potential entry points. At the same time, AI is accelerating how quickly attackers can discover vulnerabilities, identify exposed assets and turn weaknesses into opportunities for exploitation.

The result is a shrinking window for defenders. IONIX argues that the likelihood of an individual exposure being exploited has shifted dramatically. It has moved from a historically low probability (statistically safe by default) to approaching a default-breach scenario. While the exact risk varies by vulnerability and environment, the broader point is clear. Maintaining a complete inventory and validating exposures continuously are becoming essential security requirements.

IONIX has built its approach around this challenge. Through its External Exposure Management Platform, the company combines autonomous asset discovery, continuous security assessment, exploitability validation and agentic remediation. Its central premise is that if attackers operate at machine speed, defenders need to do the same.

Enterprise attack surfaces rarely stop at the boundaries of internally managed infrastructure. Vendors, cloud providers, subsidiaries and acquired businesses can introduce internet-facing assets that remain outside traditional security monitoring.

IONIX addresses this visibility gap through autonomous discovery that maps external assets, vendor-managed infrastructure and digital dependencies. The company says its platform discovers 30% to 50% more assets than competing approaches. This helps organizations identify shadow IT, overlooked applications and third-party exposures.

Through its Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM) capabilities, IONIX aims to continuously discover, monitor and prioritize exposures across an organization’s external environment. This broader visibility becomes increasingly important as enterprises adopt new technologies and expand their digital supply chains.

Identifying vulnerabilities is only part of the problem. Traditional security assessments can generate extensive findings, but not every issue represents an immediate or exploitable threat.

IONIX combines continuous security testing with non-disruptive active exploitability validation to distinguish actual exposures from theoretical risks. Its Exposure Validation capabilities examine vulnerabilities, misconfigurations and exposed technologies, testing whether identified weaknesses represent genuine security risks.

The platform then prioritizes findings according to severity, exploitability, potential blast radius and asset importance. The objective is to help security teams concentrate on exposures that present meaningful business risks rather than working through undifferentiated vulnerability lists.

IONIX is also extending exposure management beyond continuous discovery and assessment through its Live Exposure Defense solution.

The technology addresses a particularly urgent challenge: what happens when a new vulnerability is publicly disclosed? Instead of requiring security teams to manually determine which systems might be affected, IONIX automatically ingests newly published CVEs. It then correlates them against its mapped external attack surface.

The platform then uses agentic analysis to identify potentially affected assets, validate actual exploitability through safe, non-intrusive testing. It also recommends concrete mitigation measures. IONIX targets a 12-hour window from public CVE disclosure to validated exposure and actionable mitigation.

For confirmed exploitable web assets, this can include generating specific remediation workflows and mitigating actions. Specifically, it can generate Web Application Firewall (WAF) rules through supported providers such as Akamai and Cloudflare. The approach gives security teams a practical mitigation path rather than another vulnerability alert to investigate.

IONIX’s approach has attracted interest from organizations managing complex digital environments. These include Warner Music Group, BlackRock, Infosys, the Telegraph, E.ON and Grand Canyon Education.

John Remo, former SVP of Global Cloud, Infrastructure and Cybersecurity at Warner Music Group, described the platform as delivering almost immediate value without adding pressure to technical staffing. Mike Manrod, CISO at Grand Canyon Education, highlighted its ability to provide a dynamic view of an organization’s external attack surface from an attacker’s perspective.

These examples reflect a broader consideration for enterprise security buyers. The value of exposure management is not simply how many vulnerabilities a platform discovers, but whether it helps organizations understand and reduce their actual risk.

The cybersecurity market is crowded with platforms promising better visibility and vulnerability management. IONIX is pursuing a more integrated approach, bringing asset discovery, exploitability validation, risk prioritization and agentic mitigation into one continuous process.

Its focus on digital dependencies and machine-speed response addresses a growing challenge for enterprises. That challenge is keeping security controls aligned with an attack surface that never stops changing.

As AI accelerates both the discovery and exploitation of vulnerabilities, organizations will have less room to rely on incomplete inventories and periodic assessments. IONIX is betting that continuous visibility, validated exposure and faster mitigation will become fundamental requirements for the next generation of enterprise security.

Every week, I cast an eye over the latest arrivals on Prime Video, all in an effort to pick out the latest thrillers added to the streaming service library.

While November continues to be dominated by Christmas movies, I've still been able to find three worthwhile thrillers. The other two are a psychological trip and an '80s classic starring Matthew "Ferris Bueller" Broderick. Each one is worthy of your streaming consideration.

So, let's jump into the three new to Prime Video thriller movies I recommend you watch this week.

Perhaps the most “traditional” thriller among my picks this week, “Blink Twice” might not reinvent the genre, but it’s an intense watch that slowly builds tension until a shocking twist. It marked the directorial debut of Zoë Kravitz, and stars Naomi Ackie, most recently seen in “Clayface,” alongside Channing Tatum. It’s an effective first filmmaking effort from Kravitz, even if it’s perhaps not quite as intelligently plotted as the strong first act suggests.

Frida (Naomi Ackie) is a cocktail waitress at a swanky party where she meets tech tycoon Slater King (Channing Tatum). Invited to his private island for a vacation of unparalleled luxury, Frida and her friend Jess (Alia Shawkat) initially think they’ve found paradise, and Frida might have even found love with the charming tech mogul. But as lazy sun-soaked days blur into nights of glamorous partying, Frida can’t shake an uneasy feeling that something is wrong.

Three years before starring in one of the most popular movies of the 1980s, Matthew Broderick made his breakthrough with his second major feature film role. He might have made his debut in “Max Dugan Returns” in the spring of 1983. However, it was the techno-thriller “Wargames” released in the summer that saw Broderick identified as a talent to watch, and, well, those labeling him a rising star at the time were certainly proved right.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

Sure, it’s a little outdated in the 21st century, but "Wargames" is still a compelling mix of technology-driven thrills and teen drama. David Lightman (Broderick) is a gifted high schooler but with a lazy streak. A computer whiz, he uses his aptitude for computers to unknowingly access a military central computer with the ability to simulate and even launch a devastating nuclear attack against the USSR. Unaware that he’s playing with real weapons of war and thinking he’s playing a video game, he might have ignited World War III.

Rounding out my picks this week is “They Will Kill You,” a real genre-blender that mixes action, horror, comedy, and thriller elements into a movie that isn’t exactly tonally consistent, but does have quite a few slick moments. Most notably, there's a very fiery action sequence and a satisfying early reveal that flips the storyline on its head. It’s also a great showcase for Zazie Beetz, who is best known for her TV roles in “Atlanta,” “Easy” and “Invincible.”

Asia (Beetz) arrives at a posh New York City high-rise apartment building posing as a maid, but she’s really hoping to find her missing sister. Once in the complex, she discovers it’s not just home to the city's wealthy and elite, but houses a satanic cult. I’ll say no more for fear of spoiling the surprises within this action-horror, but let’s say things get very bloody, very fast. “They Will Kill You” is stylish, taking cues from Quentin Tarantino, even if it never matches the iconic director’s sharp writing and memorable characters.

#3132. Advanced Metrology for Defect Detection, Tool Health, and Semiconductor Yield Enhancement



In advanced semiconductor manufacturing, small defects can have a large effect on yield. Thin film deposition tools must stay stable and qualified. Process drift must be caught early. When a defect does appear, engineers need to know where it came from and how it affects device performance. This webinar shows how in-line inspection and offline characterization combine into one workflow, from tool monitoring to root-cause analysis.

In the first half, Dr. Bitan Chakraborty from Intel, explains how surface scan metrology fits into station monitors for thin film tools. The session shows how baseline signatures and real-time monitoring reveal hardware wear, particle generation, and process drift before they reach production wafers. It then moves to in-line scans on patterned wafers. These scans expose layer-level defects and show how they form and spread through multi-layer device stacks. Linking this defect data to electrical test results helps teams find root causes and focus their yield improvement work.

In the second half, Dr. Jacob Petersen from Evident Scientific, addresses a common question: what happens after an in-line tool flags a problem? In-line tools are fast, but they cannot always provide the details needed for a firm conclusion. Offline 3D optical profilometry fills that gap by combining three complementary inspection techniques in a single system. It delivers dimensional measurements and helps determine whether a defect lies within the sample or comes from foreign material. The session covers how several optical techniques support inspection from bare silicon to fully packaged chips. It also shows how automation enables fast measurement of features down to the sub-nanometer scale with minimal operator handling.

What You Will Learn:

  • How surface scan metrology in station monitors tracks tool health and supports the qualification of thin film deposition processes
  • How baseline signatures and real-time monitoring detect particle generation, hardware degradation, and process drift before production is affected
  • How in-line scans on patterned wafers reveal layer-level defects and show how they propagate through multi-layer device structures
  • When offline 3D optical profilometry should follow in-line inspection, and how it measures dimensions and separates sample defects from foreign material
  • How correlating tool health data, inspection results, and electrical performance links physical defects to yield loss and guides targeted improvement projects

#3131. Is SK Hynix the Better Artificial Intelligence (AI) Memory Stock Compared With Micron?

Both memory chipmakers are growing like weeds.

SK Hynix (SKHY +0.35%) and Micron (MU -0.92%) are two of the world's largest memory chipmakers. Both stocks soared as the AI boom fueled the market's demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, but they pulled back sharply over the past two months. Let's see why they cooled off -- and if either chipmaker is still worth buying as a long-term AI play.

SK Hynix, based in South Korea, is the world's second-largest producer of DRAM and NAND memory chips after Samsung. Micron, based in the U.S., ranks third in both markets. Both companies generate most of their revenue from DRAM chips rather than NAND chips.

Both companies are also relying on HBM, a specialized high-density DRAM chip that supports Nvidia's (NVDA -0.44%) data center GPUs in AI clusters, to drive their near-term growth.

SK Hynix became the first memory chipmaker to mass-produce HBM3 chips in 2022. That early-mover advantage gave it an edge over Samsung and Micron in the nascent market and put it in a prime position to profit from the AI boom over the following four years. It subsequently started producing HBM3E chips in 2024 and HBM4 chips in early 2026. SK Hynix still leads the global HBM market, while Samsung and Micron rank second and third, respectively.

Micron completely skipped the HBM3 generation, but it started mass-producing its first HBM3E chips in 2024 and made the leap to HBM4 chips in early 2026. It's also growing rapidly as the global demand for HBM chips outstrips its available supply.

As SK Hynix and Micron allocate more of their manufacturing capacity to HBM chips, they have less capacity to produce conventional DRAM and NAND chips for other markets. In other words, the accelerating production of HBM chips is causing a shortage of other memory chip types.

In 2025, SK Hynix's revenue surged 47%, its gross margin expanded year over year from 48.1% to 60.3%, and its net income soared 117%. For 2026, analysts expect its revenue to jump 275% and its net income to rise more than sixfold.

In fiscal 2026 (which ended in September), Micron's revenue more than tripled, its gross margin more than doubled to 80.7%, and its net income rose nearly tenfold. Those growth rates are incredible, but both chipmakers should see growth slow over the next two years.

Looking ahead, analysts expect SK Hynix's revenue to rise 60% in 2027 and 17% in 2028. They expect Micron's revenue to soar 107% in fiscal 2027, followed by just 16% growth in fiscal 2028 and nearly flat growth in fiscal 2029. Those longer-term estimates suggest that even though the current AI growth cycle is robust, it will inevitably cool off as the market matures.

That's why both stocks are still valued as cyclical chipmakers rather than high-growth AI stocks. SK Hynix trades at just three times this year's earnings, while Micron trades at four times this year's earnings. Several other major challenges are compressing their valuations.

First, inflation and elevated interest rates could curb AI spending and make it more difficult for smaller neocloud companies to expand. Second, the construction of new data centers in the U.S. could be more tightly regulated in several Tier-1 data center states -- including Texas, Ohio, and Georgia -- after the Democrats swept the midterm elections in early November.

SK Hynix and Micron could both experience significant volatility over the next 12 months. But if I had to pick one over the other, I'd stick with SK Hynix instead of Micron for three simple reasons: it's larger, it's growing faster, and it will remain the market leader in HBM chips.

#3130. Former Apple chairman Arthur Levinson files to sell $31.8 million in company stock

Arthur Levinson, who currently serves as Apple’s lead independent director, informed the SEC today of his plans to sell 90,000 shares of Apple stock worth approximately $31.8 million. Here are the details.

If you’ve been following Apple for a while, you likely know the name Arthur Levinson, as he served as the company’s chairman from 2011 until September of this year, when Tim Cook took over as executive chairman as part of the leadership transition that saw John Ternus become CEO.

Back in May, Levinson made headlines when he sold 250,000 Apple shares for approximately $71.2 million. Three weeks later, he sold another 50,000 shares for $15.55 million. On the same day, he also transferred another 65,000 shares as a gift. Still, he retained approximately 3.7 million directly held shares in the company.

Today, Levinson informed the SEC in a Form 144 filing of his plans to sell 90,000 common shares with an aggregate market value of $31,765,885.00, though the disclosure did not specify how many Apple shares he currently holds. The shares are held in The Homeplace Trust, with Levinson acting as trustee and handling the proposed sale on the trust’s behalf.

The filing lists all shares as acquired in cash on February 27, 2001, though it does not disclose how much Levinson originally paid for them. For reference, Apple stock was trading at approximately $0.29 per share on a split-adjusted basis on that date, compared to roughly $353 today.

Importantly, Apple has undergone three stock splits since then, meaning the 90,000 shares listed in the filing don’t necessarily correspond to the number of shares Levinson originally purchased in 2001.

According to the filing, the transaction was expected to take place today through Charles Schwab. However, it is worth noting that Form 144 is only a notice of a proposed sale, meaning the filing does not confirm that the transaction has already been completed.

#3129. OpenAI for Chile aims to train civil servants and back startups

The non-binding pact covers civil servant training and startups, with a US export scheme behind it.

OpenAI has signed a memorandum of understanding with Chile’s science ministry to explore AI in public administration, train civil servants and support local startups. The deal sets no investment or purchasing commitment, and is backed by a US Commerce Department programme that promotes American AI abroad.

OpenAI has signed an agreement with Chile’s government to bring AI into public offices and help local startups, the company announced on Tuesday. Science minister Ximena Lincolao signed for Chile at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World conference in California, where Sam Altman also spoke.

The two sides will explore using AI in the science ministry’s paperwork and training civil servants to use it safely. Startups could get help from OpenAI, including tech advice and mentoring. A joint team will set goals and a first work plan.

The deal is a non-binding pact, not a contract. The details, including what each side provides, will be agreed later. Abu Dhabi, by contrast, signed four deals with OpenAI this month, covering permits and investments.

“The MoU sets no investment or purchasing commitment,” OpenAI wrote.

The pact is backed by the US Commerce Department’s American SI Exports Program, which helps US AI firms win deals abroad. OpenAI is one of its anchor partners. Washington has also pushed federal financing for American AI exports.

Chile is the latest country to join OpenAI for Countries. Malta agreed in May to give citizens free ChatGPT Plus, and OpenAI’s head of countries, George Osborne, has courted Canada for data centres. Chile already has its own AI plan, with 177 actions across 14 ministries.
